definition: David Andreoff Evans (born 1948 in St. Louis) is an American scientist in the field of computational linguistics, best known for his research into indexing using natural language processing, and in ontology learning, especially in medical informatics.

explainer.lead: David Andreoff Evans is an American linguist.

contributions.name: He was on the faculty of Carnegie Mellon University from 1983 until 1996, and founded their Computational Linguistics Program and Laboratory for Computational Linguistics in 1986.
He has made many contributions to the field of computational linguistics and information retrieval, authoring books, many research papers, and is the holder of 25 US patents.

timeline.what: He attended the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies in 1979.
Evans attended Stanford University, receiving his Ph.D. in Computational Linguistics there in 1982.
Claritech became a research and development subsidiary of JustSystems and its name was changed to Clairvoyance Corporation in 1996, before becoming JustSystems Evans Research in 2007.
Evans was elected a Fellow of the American College of Medical Informatics in 1999. == References ==
